mutants.expected_detection: SR1 check should fail: the finding claims the feedback taps implemented are {8,7,5,4} (1-indexed) omitting the x^5 tap, whereas ground truth is that the implemented taps are {8,6,5} omitting the x^6 tap. Cross-checking the reported tap-set/description against the actual feedback expression in inputs/lfsr_rng.v (state[7]^state[5]^state[4]) shows the submission misidentifies which polynomial term is missing, so SR1's requirement that the report correctly identify the omitted x^6 tap is violated.

Evaluator's SR2 check should detect that the submission falsely claims health_error correctly detects the bias (contradicting the ground truth that health_error incorrectly remains 0), and/or that the description of the zero-crossing suppression mechanism has been removed/altered so it no longer identifies the actual root cause of the missed detection. This should cause SR2 (and likely SR4, which checks that no finding falsely claims correct detection) to fail.

evaluate.py cross-checks the reported numeric period against the iverilog/vvp-confirmed ground truth of 28 cycles (tolerance window [20,40]). This mutant reports a period of 255, implying the full maximal-length sequence, which falls far outside the acceptance window and contradicts the true short-cycle behavior caused by the missing feedback tap, so SR3 must fail.

Evaluator checks that the report does not falsely claim health_error correctly detects the bias and that the combined feedback+health-monitor finding pair has confidence >=0.5. This mutant flips the summary/finding to assert the health monitor IS working correctly (a false claim it functions properly) and drops the confidence of the combined finding pair below 0.5, burying it among low-confidence text, which should cause SR4 to fail.

evaluate.py checks that submission/trojan_report.json contains the required top-level field 'tool_version' (string) as mandated by FR1. This mutant removes the 'tool_version' field entirely from the JSON object, so schema/field-presence validation of the answer file fails, even though the findings and summary content remain otherwise correct.

Evaluator checks that at least one finding references the feedback/tap logic (the always block or continuous assignment computing the next-state feedback bit) by name or line reference as it appears in inputs/lfsr_rng.v. In this mutant, finding F1's location and description have been rewritten to reference the output-valid handshake logic (valid_logic always block / enable_seen signal) instead of the feedback_logic always block / feedback_bit expression, so no finding in the report actually references the feedback/tap computation logic at all, causing FR2 to fail even though the summary still mentions the tap defect in passing.

Evaluator checks FR3 by verifying that a finding references the health-check/repetition-monitor logic (the always block or health_error signal) by name or line reference as it appears in inputs/lfsr_rng.v. This mutant replaces the F2 finding's location/description with references to an unrelated, non-existent RTL construct ('output_mux always block, sel line 142') that does not correspond to the actual health_monitor always block or health_error signal in inputs/lfsr_rng.v, so the required health-monitor reference is absent and FR3 fails.

Evaluator extracts the reported numeric period from the findings/summary and independently confirms via iverilog/vvp simulation that the true period is 28 cycles. Since this mutant's summary and finding now state the period is 255 (the full maximal-length period) instead of ~28, this contradicts the simulation-confirmed ground truth, violating FR4 (must state the effective period as an integer consistent with observed/computed behavior) and also SR3 (must not claim the full 255-cycle sequence).
